summary: Verified the timezone/date off-by-one fix (toLocalISODate) across frontend. Static-grep confirms zero remaining `.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` occurrences in /app/frontend/src or /app/frontend/app. All required files use `toLocalISODate` correctly. Unit-style check in IST (Asia/Kolkata) confirms fix: new Date(2026,7,1)->'2026-08-01', new Date(2026,8,0)->'2026-08-31' (buggy old code would have produced '2026-07-31' and '2026-08-30' respectively — matching the user's reported symptom). Backend /api/ returns 200 with 'MakeMyEvents API'. Login screen renders on mobile viewport with 'Continue with Google' button visible. Did NOT complete OAuth per instructions.
critical_code_review_comments: AddBookingSheet.tsx line 120 uses `formatDate(date.toISOString())` for the display placeholder — safe (formatDate uses local getters so it reads back correctly), but for consistency could use toLocalISODate. Non-blocking; the submitted eventDate at line 59 correctly uses toLocalISODate.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix is code-level date formatting. To exhaustively validate end-to-end, an authenticated tester would need to (a) open Report modal, tap 'This month' preset, and confirm range shows '1 Aug 2026 → 31 Aug 2026' on the current day 23 Aug 2026 IST, and (b) create a new booking with event date = 31st of a month and confirm backend stores '2026-08-31' (not '2026-08-30'). Google OAuth (Emergent auth) blocks automated login in preview so this must be manually verified by the user or via authenticated E2E harness.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: `new Date(y, m, d).toISOString()` converts the local Date to a UTC ISO string. In IST (UTC+5:30), local midnight (00:00 IST) corresponds to 18:30 UTC of the previous day, so `.slice(0,10)` returns the previous calendar day. Fix: `toLocalISODate` uses local getters (getFullYear/getMonth+1/getDate) with zero-padding so it never round-trips through UTC. Verified by JS unit script under TZ=Asia/Kolkata: buggy code returned '2026-07-31' for 1 Aug and '2026-08-30' for 31 Aug; fixed code returns the correct '2026-08-01' and '2026-08-31'.
